body:
TUNGSTEN -- today's progress (2026-08-28)

BUILD: TUNGSTEN_10.66_APEX_QUANT_SLS(153). Naming renamed A7.5->APEX per your instruction.

Yesterday/today's TUNGSTEN_RUN package work (WARRANT#210-218):
- Step 1 (score equivalence, BLOCKING): DISAGREE -- proved the ~90min calibration search runs in a simplified score space that never touches the live scorer's real structural/adaptive layers. Real structural explanation for the standing null.
- You said "run this all day, full authority" -- WARRANT#212 shipped + live-verified: unified the calibration search to match the live scorer's formula (the single largest piece of that gap), without making the search itself too slow to run.
- WARRANT#213: tested the "bigger score = bigger move" idea directly. Does not hold on this instrument -- reported honestly rather than kept quiet.
- WARRANT#218 -- real bug, not cleanup: found that every drawdown-recovery episode this EA has EVER run was stuck at the lowest risk setting, unable to ever reach the higher settings that were already proven safe. Fixed: the risk sizing can now actually use the full range it was designed for.
- Terminal is currently NOT running -- last live run stopped mid-calibration this morning. These 4 fixes are on disk, not yet live-tested.

NEW TODAY -- FORGE FINALE campaign started:
Installed FORGE_FINALE.md (your completion definition -- 45 criteria, 8 groups) as the project's north star. Built a tracking ledger that scores real progress every session, honestly (no credit without evidence from an actual run).
Starting score: 9/45 met. After today's 2 sessions (crediting this week's real work + a new contamination check I ran for the first time): 11/45 met, 7 unknown (down from 8), 27 not met.
Ran the intraday-seasonality contamination check (Part A3) for the first time -- real seasonal pattern confirmed in the data, but it does not appear to be hiding an edge; if anything it slightly reinforces the existing null.

On your "8 weeks is too long" -- the honest lever: most of the 29 sessions need no terminal (BUILD/ANALYSIS), so I'm running them back-to-back instead of one per day via an autonomous loop, checking in with you only when a real calibration run or the edge/no-edge decision point comes up. The one part of the timeline that genuinely cannot be compressed is the final forward-validation period (weeks, by design -- no shortcuts there). Aiming to get to that stage in days, not weeks.
